title: Freedom from sin and from the law's curse
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Mosaic ceremonies stand as abrogated in Christ; forensic determinations belonging toward Jewish particular law do not bind Christians insofar as they stand as particular. — Freedom from sin's bondage stands as regeneration and sanctification, so that sin does not reign (Rom. 6). Freedom from ye law stands as from its curse and rigorous right as toward justification—not from ye moral norm.
pass_b_english: Freedom from sin's bondage is regeneration and sanctification, so that sin does not reign (Rom. 6). Freedom from the law is from its curse and rigorous right as to justification—not from the moral norm.
Mosaic ceremonies are abrogated in Christ; forensic determinations of Jewish particular law do not bind Christians insofar as they are particular.
source_text: Libertas a servitute peccati est regeneratio et sanctificatio, qua peccatum non dominatur (Rom. 6). Libertas a lege est a maledictione et rigoroso iure legis quoad iustificationem—non a norma morali. Ceremoniae Mosaicae abrogatae sunt in Christo; forenses determinationes iuris singularis populi Iudaici Christianos non adstringunt quatenus particulares.
